name: Approach C — "One responsive layout, no mobile fork" (mockup)
description:
OBJECTIVE
Build a functional HTML mockup of mobile strategy C for the codx-junior web client: instead of adding a mobile layer, delete the mobile/desktop duplication and make every screen responsive from one markup.

APPROACH C (to be prototyped)
- One `useViewport()` source of truth (breakpoints: <640 phone, 640–1024 tablet, >1024 desktop) replaces the two conflicting flags (store/ui.js width <= 1024 vs App.vue < 768).
- One responsive page shell: above 640 px the navigation is a left rail (as today on desktop), below 640 px it collapses into a drawer; the app bar exists at every width but only shows a back arrow when there is a stack.
- Screens are single-markup and use container queries (the codebase already uses `@container` + `@md:` variants) instead of `v-if="$ui.isMobile"` forks. The ChatEntry/ChatEntryMobile and GlobalSettings desktop/mobile duplication disappear.
- The dockview "desktop workspace" stays a desktop/tablet-only mode; a phone never mounts it (mobile always resolves to a single-screen route).
- Tablets get a real two-column layout (list + detail) — the mid-size case that is broken today.

REQUIRED SCREENS IN THE MOCKUP (single HTML file, three frames side by side or a width switch: 390 px, 768 px, 1280 px, dark theme)
1. Home / management dashboard rendered at all three widths from the same markup.
2. Tasks: single column list at 390, list+detail two columns at 768, board at 1280.
3. Chat: full-screen conversation at 390, list+conversation at 768/1280.
4. Global settings: one column at 390, rail + content at 768+ (this is the screen that duplicates content blocks today).
A viewport-width switcher in the mockup is required so reviewers can see the same markup reflow. One self-contained .html file (public CDN libs allowed).

DELIVERABLE PATHS
docs/mobile/strategy-C-responsive.html (self-contained) and docs/mobile/strategy-C-notes.md (max 1 page: breakpoint table, list of the components whose mobile fork gets deleted, migration order, effort estimate in days as optimistic/likely/pessimistic, top 3 risks).

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
- Visual language must match the current app: daisyUI 5 / Tailwind dark theme, FontAwesome icons.
- This is the highest-consistency / highest-effort option. The notes must state the migration cost per module and confirm the desktop dockview workspace is not impacted.

ACCEPTANCE
- The two files exist, the HTML opens standalone with no console errors, the width switcher reflows all 4 screens at 390/768/1280, and the notes contain the breakpoint table + migration order + effort range.
